findings.spf_missing: We don't see any SPF record at {host} yet. Add the TXT record from the table below.
findings.spf_multiple_records: A domain may have only one SPF record. Mail servers then honour neither. Merge them into one by adding include:amazonses.com to the existing record.

findings.spf_permissive_all: The record ends with +all, which lets anyone send. Change the ending to ~all.
findings.spf_too_many_lookups: The record has {lookups} lookups, the limit is 10. Above the limit the whole SPF record stops counting. Remove senders you no longer use.
findings.dkim_missing: We couldn't find the record {name} in DNS. Copy it from the table below.
findings.dkim_partial: We can see {found} of {expected} signatures. The remaining records are still missing or haven't propagated.
findings.dkim_wrong_value: The record {name} exists but points somewhere else.
findings.dkim_name_duplicated: It looks like the name was entered together with the domain. We found {found}. Change the name to {expected}.
findings.dkim_cloudflare_proxy: The record is proxied through Cloudflare (orange cloud). DKIM needs it turned off, switch it to DNS only.
findings.dmarc_missing: We don't see any DMARC record at {host} yet. It is optional, but we recommend it: without it you won't learn who sends in your name.
findings.dmarc_multiple_records: A domain may have only one DMARC record. We found several, keep just one.
findings.dmarc_invalid_syntax: The DMARC record can't be read, the {tag} tag is missing or malformed. Use the value from the table below.
findings.dmarc_policy_none: Your DMARC record is valid and we are leaving it alone. The p=none policy only collects reports and rejects nobody, which is right for a start. Once you have a few weeks of clean reports, tighten it to p=quarantine.
findings.dmarc_partial_pct: The policy applies to only {pct} % of messages. Set pct=100 once you are confident.
findings.dmarc_spf_alignment_strict: You have aspf=s, meaning strict SPF alignment, but you don't use a custom return address, so the SPF check will not pass. Either set aspf=r or configure a custom return address.
findings.mail_from_mx_missing: We don't see an MX record at {host} yet. Add the one from the table below.
findings.mail_from_mx_wrong: There is an MX record at {host}, but it points somewhere else.
findings.unrecognized: The value in DNS does not match the one we expect. Compare both values and fix the record at your domain administrator.

dns.cloudflareProxy: The record is proxied through Cloudflare (orange cloud). DKIM needs it turned off, switch it to DNS only.
dns.unknown: We couldn't reach the DNS server. We'll try again in a minute.
dns.spfMultiple: You have two SPF records. Mail servers ignore both in that case. Merge them into one.
dns.propagation: DNS changes usually show up within 15 minutes, rarely it takes up to 24 hours. You can close this page, we keep checking and will let you know.

help.sesSummary: Where do I get these details in AWS? Step by step
help.sesIntro: Amazon SES is an Amazon service that you run yourself. We only send through it, so the account, the access key and the domain verification all live at Amazon, not here. The steps below walk you through it from scratch. Expect about twenty minutes.
help.sesStep1Title: 1. Sign in to the AWS console
help.sesStep1Text: Open console.aws.amazon.com and sign in. If you have no Amazon account yet, create one at aws.amazon.com. Registration needs an email address, a phone number and a payment card.
help.sesStep2Title: 2. Pick a region and copy its code
help.sesStep2Text: In the top right of the console there is a dropdown with a city name, for example Frankfurt. Pick the one closest to you. The region code then shows up in the browser address bar as region=eu-central-1. Copy exactly that code, eu-central-1, into the Region field.
help.sesStep3Title: 3. Verify your sender domain or address
help.sesStep3Text: Type SES into the search box at the top, open Amazon SES and choose Identities and Create identity in the left menu. Amazon gives you DNS records to add at whoever manages your domain. Verification usually completes within an hour. Without it SES sends nothing.
help.sesStep4Title: 4. Create a user for this app
help.sesStep4Text: Type IAM into the search box, open the IAM service and choose Users and Create user. This user does not need console access, so leave the console sign-in box unchecked. Do not use the key of the main account (root), it has permissions for absolutely everything.
help.sesStep5Text: On the permissions step choose Attach policies directly and attach the ready-made AmazonSESFullAccess policy. If you want to grant the bare minimum, create your own policy with the actions ses:SendEmail, ses:GetAccount, ses:CreateEmailIdentity, ses:GetEmailIdentity and ses:PutEmailIdentityMailFromAttributes. Add ses:GetConfigurationSet, ses:CreateConfigurationSet, ses:TagResource and ses:PutConfigurationSetSuppressionOptions as well: without them we cannot create the configuration set, and without that set Amazon refuses every single message. For us to report bounces and complaints back to you, also add ses:CreateConfigurationSetEventDestination and the SNS actions sns:CreateTopic, sns:SetTopicAttributes and sns:Subscribe.
help.sesStep6Title: 6. Create the access key and copy it right away
help.sesStep6Text: Open the user you created, go to the Security credentials tab and choose Create access key. As the use case pick Application running outside AWS. Amazon then shows a pair of values: Access key ID and Secret access key. You will see the secret on that one screen and never again. Copy it immediately and paste it into the form here. If you lose it, it cannot be shown again, it can only be deleted and replaced.
help.sesRegionText: The code of an Amazon data centre, in the eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) or eu-west-1 (Ireland) format. SES is a separate service in every region, so a key, a verified domain and the limits always apply to one region only. The region here has to match the one where you verified the domain.
help.sesAccessKeyText: The public half of the access key, a bit like a username for a program. It is twenty characters long and starts with the letters AKIA. It is not secret, but on its own it is not enough.
help.sesSecretText: The secret half of the same key, in other words the password. It is forty characters long. Amazon shows it exactly once, when the key is created. We store it encrypted and the list never shows it again.
help.sesConfigSetText: A named setting inside SES that says where Amazon reports bounces, complaints and deliveries. Leave the field empty and we will create a set in your SES ourselves, named after your workspace. Fill it in only if you already have a set and want that one used.
help.sandboxTitle: A new SES account runs in test mode at Amazon
help.sandboxText: Every new SES account starts in test mode at Amazon. While it lasts, you may only send to addresses and domains verified in SES itself, at most 200 messages per 24 hours and at a rate of one message per second. This is by far the most common reason a first campaign fails to go out.
help.sandboxHowTitle: How to switch test mode at Amazon off
help.sandboxHowText: In the SES console open the Account dashboard and choose Request production access. Amazon asks who you send to and what, how people get onto your list and how you handle unsubscribes. Answer truthfully and specifically. A reply usually arrives within 24 hours. Test mode is decided per region, so after switching regions you have to ask again.
help.linkSetup: Setting up Amazon SES from scratch
help.linkRegions: List of SES regions and endpoints

help.smtpSummary: Where do I get these details?
help.smtpIntro: All four values come from whoever runs your email: your web host, your domain provider or your company administrator. Look for them in their help pages under mail settings, outgoing server or SMTP. You will find the same values in any mail program where that mailbox already works, in the account settings under outgoing mail server.
help.smtpHostText: The address of the outgoing mail server, for example smtp.wedos.net or smtp.forpsi.com. It is neither your website address nor your email address.
help.smtpPortText: The number of the door you knock on at the server. Port 587 with STARTTLS encryption is today's standard, so start there. Port 465 goes with SSL/TLS encryption. Port 25 is usually blocked by internet providers. Port 2525 is the fallback when nothing else gets through.
help.smtpUsernameText: Almost always the full email address of the mailbox, so something like post@yourcompany.com. Some hosts use a separate login name instead, which you find in the hosting administration.
help.smtpPasswordText: The password to that mailbox, not to your computer. If two-factor authentication is on at your provider, your normal password will be rejected and you have to generate a so-called app password in your account. We store the password encrypted.
help.smtpEncryptionText: This decides how the connection is secured. STARTTLS opens an unencrypted connection and immediately switches it to an encrypted one, and goes with port 587. SSL/TLS encrypts from the first second and goes with port 465. Use None only for a server on your own network, never across the internet. When in doubt, choose port 587 and STARTTLS.
help.smtpLimitText: A regular hosting plan lets through hundreds of messages a day, not tens of thousands, and starts refusing once you go over. If you plan larger sends, ask your provider about the limit before a campaign stalls half way through.

sending.domainsEmptyExplanation: The domain in your From address has to authorize us to send on its behalf. That is what the DNS records are for.

domainDialog.title: New sending domain
domainDialog.explanation: The domain is the part of your From address after the @ sign, for example kolo-shop.cz in info@kolo-shop.cz. Mail servers on the receiving end check with that domain whether we are allowed to send on its behalf. Until the domain says yes, messages end up in junk mail or get dropped outright.
domainDialog.domainHint: Enter just the domain from your From address, so kolo-shop.cz. No www, no https:// and no trailing slash.
domainDialog.providerLabel: Which sending account will be used
domainDialog.providerHint: A domain belongs to one account. The DNS records we show you next are built from it.
domainDialog.providerSingle: We will attach the domain to the {name} account, the only one you have so far.
domainDialog.noProviders: You need a sending account first. A domain is registered to the account your emails go out from, so without one there is nothing to attach it to. Close this window and use the Add sending account button.
domainDialog.nextStep1: We show you the finished DNS records: type, name and value. You invent nothing, you only copy them over.
domainDialog.nextStep2: You add the records wherever your domain is managed. That is usually the company you pay for the domain, the registrar, or your web host. In their interface look for DNS, DNS records or domain management.
domainDialog.nextStep3: Then you come back here and press Check now. We look whether the records are visible and tell you what is still missing.
domainDialog.timingText: A new record spreads across the internet within minutes, rarely it takes a few hours. That is normal, not a fault. You can close the page and come back to the check whenever you like.
domainDialog.submitUnavailable: A domain cannot be added without a sending account.
domainDialog.invalidDomain: That does not look like a domain. Enter it as kolo-shop.cz.
domainDialog.tooLong: The domain must not be longer than {max} characters.
domainDialog.failed: We could not add the domain.

deleteDomainDialog.title: Remove the domain {domain}?
deleteDomainDialog.explanation: The domain disappears from the list and you won't be able to start new campaigns from it until you add it again.
deleteDomainDialog.sesStays: At Amazon the domain stays verified. We don't delete its identity, because the same Amazon account may be used by another project. It will be reused if you add the domain again.
deleteDomainDialog.dnsStays: Leave the DNS records at your registrar alone. They break nothing, and without them the domain would have to be verified from scratch if you add it again. Remove them only once you really stop using the domain for sending.
deleteDomainDialog.historyStays: Sent campaigns and their statistics stay, you won't lose the numbers.
deleteDomainDialog.trialWarning: This is your only verified domain. After removing it the project falls back to trial mode and email will only go to verified addresses.
deleteDomainDialog.runningCampaigns: If a campaign is running or scheduled through the domain, removing it won't work. Finish or cancel the campaign first.
deleteDomainDialog.inUse: The domain can't be removed because a campaign is running or scheduled through it. Finish or cancel it and try again.
deleteDomainDialog.hasCampaigns: The domain can't be removed because {count, plural, =0 {no campaign holds} one {# campaign holds} other {# campaigns hold}} it. Sent campaigns keep the domain for the record, so you have to delete them permanently before removing it.
deleteDomainDialog.conflict: The domain can't be removed because something is using it.
deleteDomainDialog.forbidden: You don't have permission to remove a sending domain. Ask a project administrator.
deleteDomainDialog.notFound: The domain no longer exists, someone probably removed it in the meantime.

region.label: Amazon region
region.unknownOption: {code}, a stored region outside our list
region.consoleName: In the AWS console this region is called {awsName}.
region.optInNote: Amazon has it turned off for new accounts, so enable it in your AWS account settings first.
region.warningTitle: The region has to match what you set up in Amazon SES
region.warningIntro: Amazon keeps everything separately per region. Only in the one you pick here do these apply:
region.boundIdentities: verified addresses and domains you are allowed to send from,
region.boundSandbox: the account test mode, meaning whether Amazon delivers to anyone or only to verified addresses,
region.boundQuota: the daily limit and the allowed sending rate,
region.boundConfigSet: the configuration set, without which Amazon rejects every single message,
region.boundDkim: the DKIM records you put into your domain's DNS.
region.whereToFind: You find the region in the AWS console at the top right, where a city name is shown, for example Frankfurt. Its short code is also in the browser address bar, in the region=eu-central-1 part. Pick the same one here that you verified your domain or address in.
region.changeTitle: You are changing the region from {from} to {to}
region.changeConfigSet: Amazon has no configuration set in the new region. We create it ourselves during the next connection test, but until that runs, not a single message goes out.
region.changeIdentities: Verified addresses and domains do not move between regions. Whatever is verified in the old region stays there.
region.changeDkim: The domain's DKIM records only apply to the region they were created in. The domain will need verifying again and different values will go into DNS.
region.changeSandbox: Test mode and production access are counted separately per region. Even if you were granted production access in the old region, the account will be back in test mode in the new one.
region.changeAfter: After saving we run a connection test. It creates the configuration set and tells you straight away what is missing in the new region.

regionFacts.inRegion: The account is in the {region} region.
regionFacts.identitiesUnknown: We could not find out what you have verified there with Amazon.
regionFacts.identitiesNone: You have no verified address and no verified domain there.
regionFacts.identitiesSomeMore: Verified there: {list} and {rest, plural, =0 {nothing else} one {# more} other {# more}}.
regionFacts.nothingTitle: Nothing will go out like this
regionFacts.nothingText: Amazon keeps the account in test mode and in the {region} region you have no verified address or domain. In that state it rejects even a test email to your own address. Verify an address with the button next to the account, or switch the account to a region where you already have something verified.

identity.title: Verify an address with Amazon, account {name}
identity.explanation: Amazon only delivers from addresses and domains it has verified. You can verify an address right here, there is no need to go to the Amazon console for it.
identity.regionNote: Verification will happen in the {region} region, exactly where this account sends from. It will not apply in any other region.
identity.whoSends: The confirmation email is sent by Amazon, not by us. It arrives from Amazon Web Services and the link inside is only valid for a limited time, so open it right away. The address becomes verified only once somebody clicks that link.
identity.failed: We could not start the verification.
identity.resultVerified: Done. Amazon will let you send from this address.
identity.resultPending: Amazon sent a confirmation link to the address. Open it and then check the status here.
identity.resultAlreadyExisted: The account already knows this address in this region, so no new confirmation email was sent. If it is still unconfirmed, find the original message from Amazon, or delete the address in the AWS console and create it again.

state.temporary_failure: Amazon could not tell right now

productionAccess.title: Request production access, account {name}
productionAccess.explanation: While the account is in test mode, Amazon only delivers to verified addresses. You can submit the request for production access right from here.
productionAccess.regionNote: The request only applies to the {region} region. In every other region the account stays in test mode even after approval.
productionAccess.whatAmazonWants: Amazon will want to know this:
productionAccess.wantsMailType: whether you send marketing or transactional mail,
productionAccess.wantsWebsite: your website address, so it knows what will be sent,
productionAccess.wantsContact: optionally another contact address it can reach you at.
productionAccess.review: The request is reviewed by a person from AWS support. The first answer comes within 24 hours.
productionAccess.noEditsDuringReview: Until the review is finished you cannot change the details or submit a second request.
productionAccess.mailTypeMarketingHint: Newsletters, offers, campaigns. For sending to your contacts this is the usual choice.
productionAccess.mailTypeTransactionalHint: Order confirmations, password resets, notices triggered by the recipient's own action.
productionAccess.websiteHint: For example https://kolo-shop.cz. Amazon uses it to judge what will be sent.
productionAccess.contactHint: Amazon can send questions about the request to it.
productionAccess.sent: The request is in. Amazon is reviewing it now and sends the answer to the account contact address, usually within 24 hours.
productionAccess.required: This field needs to be filled in.
productionAccess.failed: We could not submit the request.
productionAccess.alreadyUnderReview: Amazon is already reviewing one of your requests. You cannot submit another until that one is finished.

editDialog.title: Edit account {name}
editDialog.explanation: We can't show you the stored credentials again, we only keep them encrypted. Leave the key and password fields empty unless you want to replace them.
editDialog.name: Account name
editDialog.nameHint: For your orientation in the list only. Recipients never see it.
editDialog.secretAccessKeyHint: Fill this in only when you are replacing the key. An empty field leaves it as it is.
editDialog.passwordHint: Fill this in only when you are changing the password. An empty field leaves it as it is.
editDialog.secretHint: Currently stored: {current}. Fill this in only when you want to change it.
editDialog.required: This field needs to be filled in.
editDialog.tooLong: Must not be longer than {max} characters.
editDialog.regionRequired: Pick a region. It has to be the one where your domain or address is verified with Amazon.
editDialog.rotatePair: The access key ID and the secret access key are issued as a pair. When you change one, fill in both.
editDialog.noChanges: You haven't changed anything, so there is nothing to save.
editDialog.failed: The changes could not be saved.

deleteDialog.title: Remove account {name}?
deleteDialog.explanation: Removing it deletes the stored credentials for good. Campaigns waiting to be sent through this account will have nothing to send them with.
deleteDialog.historyStays: Sent campaigns and their statistics stay, you won't lose any numbers.
deleteDialog.runningCampaigns: While a campaign is running or scheduled on this account, it cannot be removed. Finish or cancel the campaign first.
deleteDialog.defaultWarning: This is the default sending account. Once removed, no default is left and a new campaign will have nothing to send from until you pick another one.
deleteDialog.conflict: The account cannot be removed because a campaign is running or scheduled on it. Finish or cancel it and try again.
deleteDialog.forbidden: You don't have permission to remove a sending account. Ask a project administrator.
deleteDialog.notFound: The account no longer exists, someone else has probably removed it in the meantime.
deleteDialog.failed: The account could not be removed.

verify.ok: Verified. The credentials work and the provider answered our question.
verify.statusUnknown: We could not read the account state, so we are not claiming anything about its readiness to send yet.
verify.failed: The check failed and the account will not send like this.

reasons.credentials: Amazon rejected the access keys. Check the access key ID and the secret access key, or create a new pair in the AWS console and paste it here.
reasons.permissions: The key is valid, but the user lacks permissions. Grant it ses:GetAccount, ses:SendEmail, ses:GetEmailIdentity and ses:CreateConfigurationSet in the AWS console.
reasons.region: The region doesn't match. Check that it reads like eu-central-1 and that SES is actually enabled there.
reasons.network: Amazon did not answer. This looks like a temporary connection outage, try the check again in a moment.
reasons.unknown: Amazon rejected the check without telling us why. The details from its response are below.

codes.provider_smtp_auth_failed: The SMTP server rejected the user name or password. Check the credentials from your e-mail provider.
codes.provider_smtp_host_unknown: The server address could not be resolved. Check it for typos.
codes.provider_smtp_connection_refused: The server refused the connection. Check the port and whether your provider allows sending from elsewhere at all.
codes.provider_smtp_tls_invalid: The encrypted connection could not be established. Try a different encryption setting, usually STARTTLS on port 587.
codes.provider_smtp_timeout: The server did not answer in time. Check the port and try again in a moment.
codes.provider_smtp_starttls_unsupported: The server does not offer STARTTLS. Switch encryption to SSL/TLS, usually on port 465.
codes.provider_smtp_greeting_invalid: There is no SMTP server answering at this address and port. Check both.

blockers.provider_disabled: The account is turned off by hand. It will not send anything until you turn it back on.
blockers.credentials_invalid: The credentials are not valid. Enter them again, or create new ones with your provider.
blockers.sending_disabled: The provider has sending from this account turned off. Find out why in your AWS console.
blockers.enforcement_shutdown: Amazon has paused the account. Sending cannot start until you sort it out with them.
blockers.configuration_set_missing: The configuration set is missing at Amazon and without it not a single message goes out. Run the connection test and we will create it.
blockers.configuration_set_error: The configuration set could not be created at Amazon. The key most likely lacks the ses:CreateConfigurationSet permission.
blockers.domain_not_verified: Amazon has not verified any of your sending domains yet. Open the domain and check its DNS records.
blockers.enforcement_probation: Amazon has the account under review because of bounces or complaints. You can send, but carefully.
blockers.events_pending: Amazon has not confirmed the event subscription yet, so we do not learn about bounces or complaints. This does not block sending.
blockers.events_not_configured: Delivery and bounce reporting is not set up at Amazon.
blockers.events_error: Delivery and bounce reporting could not be set up at Amazon. This does not block sending.
blockers.sandbox: Amazon keeps the account in test mode, so it only delivers to addresses verified directly with them. You can verify an address right here, and request production access here too.
blockers.sandbox_no_identities: In the region we send from you have no verified address and no verified domain at Amazon. In test mode nothing goes out at all, not even a test email to your own address. Verify an address with the button next to the account, or switch the account to the region where you already have something verified.
blockers.dmarc_missing: DMARC is missing or wrong on one of the domains. You can send, but deliverability suffers.

thresholds.title: Deliverability guards
thresholds.explanation: These numbers stop a campaign before Amazon does. The value from the installation is both the default and the ceiling, so you can only make a guard stricter, never looser.
thresholds.bounceGuard: Pause at a bounce rate of
thresholds.complaintGuard: Pause at a complaint rate of
thresholds.bounceWarn: Warn at a bounce rate of
thresholds.complaintWarn: Warn at a complaint rate of
thresholds.minSent: Evaluate only after this many messages
thresholds.tooLoose: You can only set a stricter value. The ceiling is {max}.

smtpWarning: A plain SMTP server can't report undelivered mail and complaints to us. You have to maintain the blocked address list yourself.

senders.title: Senders
senders.subtitle: Saved sets of sender details. Pick one on a campaign and the name, address, reply-to address, account and domain fill themselves in.
senders.replyToSame: Replies go to the sender address
senders.emptyExplanation: Most campaigns go out under the same name and from the same address. Save them once and just pick them on every campaign after that.
senders.noDomainsExplanation: A sender is built on a verified domain, because that is what the mail is sent from. Without one there is nothing to build it from.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this sender?
deleteDialog.explanation: The preset {name} will disappear from the list on campaigns.
deleteDialog.campaignsSafe: Sent and draft campaigns are not affected. Their sender details stay stored and they keep sending exactly as before.

dialog.explanation: This is a preset, not a sending setting. The values only pre-fill a campaign and can be overwritten there at any time without changing the preset.
dialog.name: Preset name
dialog.nameHint: For you only, so you can tell presets apart in the list. It never reaches the e-mail.
dialog.domainHint: It also determines the sending account: every domain belongs to exactly one.
dialog.domainUnverified: This domain is not verified with Amazon yet. You can save the preset, but a campaign cannot be sent from it until verification finishes.
dialog.fromNameHint: What the recipient sees instead of the address, for example your company name.
dialog.fromEmailHint: The address has to belong to the selected sending domain, otherwise the e-mails end up in spam.
dialog.fromEmailHintDomain: The address has to be on the {domain} domain, otherwise the e-mails end up in spam.
dialog.replyToHint: Leave empty if the sender address is enough. This one may sit outside the sending domain.
dialog.isDefaultHint: A new campaign is pre-filled from the default preset. Only one can be the default.
dialog.noDomains: You have no sending domain. Add one in the sending settings and come back here.
dialog.invalidEmail: This does not look like an e-mail address.
dialog.outsideDomain: The address has to be on the {domain} domain.
dialog.submitUnavailable: Without a sending domain there is nothing to build a sender from.

picker.label: Saved sender
picker.hint: Picking one overwrites the fields below and saves them right away, including anything you have typed there. You can still edit them by hand afterwards without touching the preset.
picker.empty: You have no saved sender yet, so fill the fields below in by hand. Save them once and you will just pick them from the list on every campaign after that.
picker.failed: The preset could not be applied. Please try again.
